history.summary: The tokens that let a theme have a type voice, and the re-pointing pass that makes them real. registry/tokens/typography.css now separates the PALETTE (--font-sans/-serif/-mono) from the ROLES components read (--font-heading/-body/-ui) and adds the four heading-voice knobs (--heading-weight/-tracking/-transform/-leading). Every consumer moved: 72 family references across 64 stylesheets, classified by role rather than renamed in bulk — controls and floating chrome to --font-ui (44), content surfaces to --font-body (17), headings to --font-heading, and the eleven var(--doc-font, …) chains keeping the document face first with the body role as their floor. Ten heading surfaces that only inherited a family now name the role (card/dialog/drawer/sheet/alert-dialog/callout/empty-state titles, the stat value, every pattern headline). --heading-tracking is 0em, not the plan's 0: calc(-0.01em + 0) is invalid CSS and would have silently dropped the heading primitive's optical tightening; with a unit, a theme's tracking ADDS to a heading's own. No visual change was measured, not argued — every canonical fragment rendered in Chromium before and after, all six type properties compared element by element: 4,160 elements x 6 readings, four differences, all one deliberate fix (a callout and a page-break inside a data-variant="report" document used to render sans inside a serif page, because the variant set font-family while they read var(--doc-font, …); the variant now re-points --doc-font for its subtree). gen:theme-manifests produced 84 pure insertions across 12 manifests with zero deletions — tokens_inherited only. The docs generator needed real work: it derived a token's preview property from its name prefix, which the heading-* family breaks (each drives a different property), so HEADING_VOICE_PROPERTY names them and the typography page grew a Font roles section and a Heading voice section. tests/tokens/role-tokens.test.ts (28 cases) is the permanent gate.

The baseline was intermittently red and the engine was innocent: tests that assert on work a MutationObserver delivers were spending a FIXED number of await tick()s waiting for it. The main partition shares one process and one happy-dom realm, so a late file inherits ~170 files' worth of pending effects and timers, and the delivery lands a turn further out than the test allowed. Measured on a clean tree at 1f36b0f: tests/recipes/tree-view-reactive.test.ts failed 3 full-suite runs in 4 (aria-posinset "1" where the reorder makes it "2"), tests/core/lifecycle.test.ts's late-append l-cloak case took the fourth — every one of them green alone, green in its own directory, green with tests/core/ alone; bisection found no single polluting file, only the accumulated queue, which is exactly what a tick count cannot be calibrated against. happy-dom delivers observer callbacks on a real microtask (MutationObserverListener.report → window.queueMicrotask), so the waits were not wrong in principle, only in assuming one turn is always enough. tests/helpers/settle.ts adds settle(condition, what, turns): poll one turn at a time, return the moment the condition holds (the already-satisfied path costs no turns), throw naming the awaited behavior when the 50-turn budget runs out, and treat a throwing probe as not-settled so a test can address a node the pending work has yet to create. The two flakes now wait for the refresh instead of for a turn; lifecycle.test.ts's 'two turns' comment, which predicted this exact failure, is gone with it. tests/meta/settle.test.ts (11 cases) is the permanent gate, in the two halves spawn-timeouts.test.ts uses: behavioural proof that settle() waits, returns early and fails legibly, plus a source gate over tests/ and packages/ banning any NEW consecutive await tick() pair. Six older boot/mount helpers (faqir-mask, inbox, engine-page — two each) are allow-listed rather than converted blind, each needs a condition chosen by someone reading what it boots, and the gate fails in BOTH directions so a converted site must be delisted instead of the list becoming documentation of a habit. The gate was proven non-vacuous by planting a pair and watching it go red. Verification: 5 full-suite runs, 4 green (207 files); run 2's single failure was a 60s spawn budget expiring with empty stdout while bun run typecheck's seven tsc passes competed for the machine, and run 3 hit the runner's 20-minute partition cap having printed no test output at all — a bun-level wedge before any file reported, the class commit c2fc2d7 already names. Neither is this suite's assertion timing, and the flake this task targets did not recur once. Found while verifying 1.1A-02's baseline, which is why 1.1A-02 did not run.

The two families a theme needs to state a silhouette and a ring. registry/tokens/effects.css publishes the shape ladder (--border-width-sm/-md/-lg), the two ROLES components name (--border-width, --border-width-strong), --corner-shape, and the five focus tokens (--focus-ring-width/-offset/-style/-color, --focus-shadow) — 11 tokens, 13 with the --card-border-width / --input-border-width silhouette aliases 1.1A-05 will aim at; the theme surface moved 241 → 254 and gen:theme-manifests produced 156 PURE insertions across 12 manifests, zero deletions. base/reset.css's :focus-visible spells out nothing any more, and the gate fails on a bare length or colour appearing in it. Every literal edge in the primitives is gone: 40 border widths in 22 files and 13 outlines in 13 files, classified rather than renamed in bulk — the default edge to --border-width (including the four forced-colors rules), emphasis to --border-width-strong where the design leans on a thicker rule (kbd's keycap bottom, nav's active indicator, separator[data-weight=thick], collapsible's chevron, the spinner ring and button[data-state=loading]'s), --border-width-lg for the spinner's 3px, and the alias on card/input/textarea/select. --focus-shadow is consumed in reset AND in all 13 primitive rings, because a control's own :focus-visible (0,2,0) outranks reset's (0,1,0) — declared only in reset the glow axis would have reached bare elements and no button. The inset rings read calc(-1 * var(--input-border-width)) so the ring keeps covering the edge when a theme thickens it. No visual change was MEASURED: every registry fragment rendered in Chrome 149 before and after with every focus rule forced on, four border sides plus outline width/style/offset and box-shadow compared element by element — 4,093 elements x 8 readings, ZERO differences; corner-shape is supported by that engine and computes to its initial `round` on all six surfaces. Two shim findings shaped the CSS: happy-dom drops any border shorthand resolving to an oklch() colour (so the in-suite proof swaps colours for hex), and it mis-splits var(--a, var(--b)) in a shorthand's width slot, which is why the aliases are named at one level. tests/tokens/shape-focus.test.ts (38 cases) is the permanent gate, proven non-vacuous by planting a literal; tests/base/prose.test.ts's value index needed the shape and focus families excluded — left in, --border-width-md: 2px claimed prose's text-underline-offset.

The sweep 1.1A-02 started, finished: base, recipes and patterns read the shape and focus families, and the gate is now registry-wide. 150 declarations in 31 stylesheets, classified rather than renamed in bulk — 92 literal border widths (1px to --border-width, 2px to --border-width-strong, 3px to --border-width-lg), 29 literal rings to var(--focus-ring-width) var(--focus-ring-style) var(--focus-ring-color), and 29 literal outline offsets, the inset ones as calc(-1 * var(--focus-ring-offset)) and table's filter input as calc(-1 * var(--border-width)), because that ring is inset by exactly the edge it covers. Five more rings were invisible to 1.1A-02's gate because they were not literals: context-menu, tree-view and file-upload drew theirs out of the SPACING family (var(--space-px), calc(var(--space-px) * 2)), which is how three components had a 1px ring while every other control had 2px. Eight declarations are deliberately not tokenised — table's sort arrow and expander caret are CSS triangles whose three border legs ARE the glyph — and they are named rule by rule in GLYPH_RULES, with a test asserting the sweep skips those four rules and nothing else. The emphasis role reaches all seven rules that lean on a thicker rule (pricing featured tier, tabs underline indicator, stepper connector, table header + footer rules, settings rail marker, slider thumb), two of which are not borders at all: the connector is a height and the featured tier is an outline, which is why the gate states the converse rule — an outline inside a :focus rule is a ring and reads the focus family, an outline anywhere else is an edge and reads the shape family. tabs' forced-colors selection indicator moved across that line to --border-width-strong with the OS Highlight colour. Measured, not argued: 18 cases resolve each re-pointed family's declaration, read out of the shipped stylesheet, against the literal it carried at 375d247; six of those rules are logical and happy-dom implements no logical border longhand, so the width slot is re-declared on border-top, which also sidesteps the shim's comma-split on a var() with a fallback. Five widths changed on purpose, all upward to what the rest of the registry already used: pricing's featured tier 1px to 2px and the four hairline rings 1px to 2px with their offsets. The gate grew 38 to 65 cases, scans rule by rule so an allow-list can be stated in selectors, and blanks comments instead of deleting them so a reported line number is real — proven by planting border: 1px in dialog.css and getting recipes/dialog/dialog.css:38 back. 35 manifests and headers updated additively (the headers are hand-curated, so a recompute would have rewritten 29 sheets' worth of curation); the pre-existing header/tokens_used drift stayed at exactly the same 29 files. Two older tests asserted the literal spelling and moved to the token one: responsive-canon's auth-form card edge and prose's header rule.

The two axes 1.0 left a theme no handle on. registry/tokens/effects.css publishes --shadow-color as BARE OKLCH channels (0 0 0, not oklch(0 0 0)) so each of the five ramp steps still sets its own alpha; all ten layers read it, and one declaration re-tints the lot. --surface-backdrop: none is consumed by nine surfaces — card, surface[data-variant=overlay] and the seven floating recipes, tooltip hooked on its content rule since it draws no shadow — each inside the same @supports guard themes/glass.css uses, with the -webkit- prefix beside the standard property, so glass becomes tokens in 1.1A-14 instead of a theme reaching into seven components by selector. New registry/tokens/textures.css ships six named currentColor SVG data URIs; components read only the two roles in aliases.css (--texture-page on body and document, --texture-surface on surface, card, hero). index.css imports it and so do the FOUR other hand-maintained cascade-order lists that cannot be globbed (bundler, init, build-core-package, visual matrix) — density.test.ts is what catches a missed one. textures.css is NOT themeable surface: it is a palette no component reads, so a theme re-points a role instead of inheriting six data URIs; gen:theme-manifests produced 48 PURE insertions across 12 manifests, zero deletions, and not one URI. Surface 254 -> 258. The literal-shadow census was 8; the gate found FOURTEEN. The eight are all rings (0 0 0 w colour) and split by the converse of 1.1A-03's rule — a ring in a :focus* rule reads the focus family (menubar, combobox, tag-input), a ring expressing a STATE keeps its semantic colour and takes its width from the shape family (field-group x3, input-otp, file-upload, the last drawing its from the SPACING family). The other six hid inside var(--shadow-*, …) FALLBACKS — document (two rgba layers), stat, tabs, slider (three, plus two colour halos) — all deleted rather than re-tokenised, since the token layer always defines them and the fallback only served to hide an untintable colour. Five background: shorthands became background-color: so they would stop resetting the texture the base rule had just set; no such element declares another background longhand, which is why it is a no-op. No shadow alias was added: every floating recipe already read the ramp, so the plan's --popover-shadow would have been indirection with no consumer. No visual change was MEASURED, not argued: all 85 fragments rendered in Chromium before and after, 3,711 elements x 11 readings = 40,821 comparisons, ZERO differences — and the reverse proved too, a theme setting all four puts grain on body, dots on card and hero, blur(16px) saturate(1.4) on the overlay/card/dialog panel, and tints the whole ramp warm. Two guards outside Touches moved because growing the surface is what breaks them: theme generate now emits --shadow-color and re-points its own ramp at it (declaring a channel it did not read would be the dead-axis drift 1.1A-21 tracks) and keeps it a valid colour in document themes, since oklch(none / 0.04) is not CSS; theme-coverage excludes it from the required set for the opposite reason — a dark block that omits it inherits 0 0 0, exactly what an untinted dark theme wants. tests/tokens/depth-material.test.ts (60 cases) is the permanent gate, proven non-vacuous by planting a literal shadow in dialog.css and a broken texture URI. Ran after 1.1A-23 quarantined the tree-view flake that had made the baseline red for this session's first four full-suite runs.

The three axes 1.0 left a theme no handle on, and the namespace rule they taught. 22 tokens, surface 258 -> 280, gen:theme-manifests 264 PURE insertions across 12 manifests with zero deletions. Motion: --ease-spring joins the easing PALETTE beside --ease-bounce (no consumer since 1.0 either, because a palette is re-pointed rather than read), declared cubic-bezier-FIRST with the linear() upgrade inside @supports (animation-timing-function: linear(0, 1)) -- a custom property stores whatever tokens it is given, so an unguarded spring is ACCEPTED by a browser without linear() and then drops every transition that used it, landing on the initial easing rather than on a fallback. --motion-hover-lift is `none`, the initial value of `translate`, not the plan's -1px: neither button nor card lifted before this task, so a length default would move every button in every project, and `translate` rather than `transform` so a component's own transform is never clobbered. Decoration: the three --link-*, --divider-style, --stripe-bg, the two --selection-* and --marker-color (currentColor, ::marker's initial colour, not the plan's accent). The link family reaches FIVE surfaces, not the one named: link itself, prose a, and the three hover affordances that spelled text-decoration: underline (button[data-variant=link], breadcrumb, auth-form footer), so --link-decoration: none silences every underline at once. reset.css owns ::selection, the one surface of a themed page that never matched the theme. Controls: --button-text-transform, --input-fill (read by input, textarea AND select, so one declaration fills every text control) + --input-bg-filled -- NOT the plan's `--input-fill: none`, which cannot fall through to --input-bg since var() only takes a fallback for an UNDEFINED property. The easing sweep found the registry already clean except for two literals hiding exactly where 1.1A-04's six hid: in var(--duration-fast, 120ms) var(--ease-default, ease) FALLBACKS (input-otp, slider), deleted. `linear` survives by NAME at six sites, each asserted exhaustively: two faqir-spin rotations (a spinner that eases stutters once per turn) and four `visibility 0s linear` steps. THE NAMESPACE FINDING shaped the CSS: naming one token --checkbox-radius makes --checkbox-* a token FAMILY and audit:registry then reads all 21 other --checkbox-/--switch-/--table- references as tokens wearing a fallback as a disguise. For checkbox and switch that obligation is worth meeting (static default geometry, declared, redundant fallbacks deleted); for table it is not -- --table-level is stamped and --table-thead-h is MEASURED per element by the controller -- so the zebra is --stripe-bg, not the plan's --table-stripe. No visual change was MEASURED, not argued: all 85 fragments rendered in Chromium 149 before and after, 3,711 elements x 19 readings = 70,509 comparisons, 21 differences, every one the `transition` property on the two surfaces that gained a hover rule, both pixel-inert by construction. Two surfaces the fragment sweep cannot reach carry the only DELIBERATE changes: prose a's underline offset 2px -> 3.2px, unifying it with the link primitive's 0.2em (the two had drifted; one role token cannot hold both), and ::selection now themed rather than OS-drawn. Converse proved too: a theme setting the eleven axes gets uppercase buttons, a 0 -2px lift, undecorated links, dashed dividers, a filled input, a squared checkbox, a 2px switch, accented markers and a real linear() spring. density.css untouched and the drift test says why -- it DERIVES the dependent set, and not one of the 22 reads --space-* or --control-height-*. card.css gained its own prefers-reduced-motion block, which the pristine-project audit caught the moment card began to transition. tests/tokens/motion-decoration-controls.test.ts (41 cases) is the permanent gate; the non-vacuity proof earned its keep -- the first easing sweep sailed past a planted cubic-bezier() because a \b after a closing paren never matches. 1.1A-04's ramp gate moved with it: it matched var(--shadow as TEXT, so it now resolves one alias level and follows --switch-thumb-shadow: var(--shadow-xs) to the ramp. --motion-stagger and --motion-blur were DECLINED for want of any consumer and recorded as follow-up 1.1A-24.

A theme may now state both schemes in one :root block, and every browser-free gate reads that form exactly as a browser resolves it. base/reset.css declares the cascade contract once — :root is color-scheme: light, [data-theme="dark"] is dark, [data-theme="auto"] is light dark — because light-dark() reads color-scheme, not data-theme, and nothing in the registry declared it before (asserted registry-wide, print blocks excepted). substituteLightDark() resolves a call ANYWHERE in a value, splitting at the TOP-LEVEL comma so light-dark(var(--a, red), var(--b)) keeps red on the light side; a malformed call is left verbatim so the gates see the value a browser would also reject. THE MODEL FINDING: a scheme is not a BLOCK. --color-surface-1: var(--color-bg-subtle) needs no dark spelling because the token it reads already has one, so the parser derives scheme-awareness to a fixpoint — a :root declaration counts for dark and auto if it uses light-dark(), or if every var() it names is itself scheme-aware; a literal never does, which is exactly the gap coverage exists for. Without it the migrated default had four uncovered tokens and the only honest fix would have been light-dark(x, x), which states nothing. An explicit block still outranks the function, mirroring the cascade. parseThemeSchemes is now parseThemeValues with a name filter — one parser, so the coverage model and the contrast audit cannot disagree about which block a declaration belongs to. default.css went 80 declarations to 41: 31 colours stated ONCE where the file stated 8 in :root and 36 twice more, and gen:theme-manifests reproduced all 12 manifests byte-identically (tokens_overridden was already the union of names). MEASURED, not argued: tests/browser/light-dark.pw.ts renders the migrated sheet and the v1.0.0 sheet (git show, never pasted) in Chromium 149 and compares every --color-* as background-color, every --shadow-* as box-shadow, plus html's colour/background/color-scheme and a live button and card, across light, dark and auto under both emulated preferences — 172 comparisons, ZERO differences. Non-vacuous in both directions: deleting one rule from the cascade contract turns the dark case red, and a separate case proves the four scheme states are not one reading. THE SHADOW RAMP DID NOT COLLAPSE and the reason is load-bearing: light-dark() is a <color> function and a shadow list is not a colour, so a step whose schemes differ in geometry (none against two layers) has no honest one-block spelling — the per-layer form would pad the dark ramp with alpha-0 layers, writing a shadow where the theme says none. It keeps its blocks in both authoring forms; light stays inherited from effects.css. THE COST the one-block form creates is gated, not hoped for: a token cannot read its own base value (light-dark(var(--color-bg), …) on --color-bg is a cycle), so the single block restates the light value it used to inherit; tests/themes/light-dark.test.ts (13 cases) compares every restated light argument against semantic/effects and lists the four deliberate AA corrections, failing in BOTH directions. The generator merges the two lists for --scheme both (identical values emitted plainly), keeps a six-declaration shadow dark block, and --legacy-blocks restores the three-block colour form; the two forms are proven the same theme — identical manifest, identical contrast report, identical per-scheme token sets — which is a real cross-check because the render paths differ. ONE DEVIATION from the plan's Tests block, recorded: a generated both theme DOES contain a [data-theme="dark"] block (the six shadow declarations), so the assertion is that no --color-* reaches one, plus set-equality on what does. Two focus-ring non-vacuity proofs moved because they planted a regression into a bare --color-ring: oklch(…) and would have matched nothing against a light-dark() pair — the plant now rewrites every oklch() in the declaration and asserts it changed something. tests/utils/light-dark.test.ts (17 cases) is the parser gate. check:manifest-api's recipes/table staleness was verified pre-existing at 20953e2.

The theme manifest learns to carry a seed, and the schema moves inside the freeze. manifest.schema.json goes 1.0 -> 1.1 in 555 insertions and THREE replaced lines (schema_version, the document description, the theme definition's), so the diff reads as what it is. Five optional fields on themeManifest — seed, axes, fonts, distinctiveness, visual_matrix — and nine new definitions behind them: themeSeed, themeAxes, the four composite axes (themeAxisType/Shape/Decoration/Controls, plus themeAxisVoice nested in the first) and themeFont/themeDistinctiveness. 23 enumerated axes and 24 defaults; the schema's enum count went 6 to 38. THE FREEZE IS ASSERTED POSITIVELY, not assumed: themeManifest.required is compared against the 1.0 list verbatim and each new field checked absent from it; all 98 shipped manifests still validate; no shipped theme gained a field, because seed/axes land in 1.1A-08 and 1.1A-11. SCHEMA_VERSION is now the number PROTOCOL_VERSION is not, and protocol-1.0.test.ts gained a case that says so out loud — the two differ, every changelog row after the freeze is non-breaking, and §8's 'add an optional field to the manifest schema / additive' row is the licence §9's last row claims; without that a schema bump is a number nobody checked. THE VOCABULARY EXISTS TWICE AND NEITHER COPY IS DECORATIVE: the schema states it for whatever resolves the published contract, src/theme-manifest.ts states it for the CLI's own validateThemeManifest (which now validates a seed axis by axis, rejecting a misspelled one rather than ignoring it — a typo'd axis is a theme that silently comes out wrong), and the drift test walks both to dotted paths and compares them, proven non-vacuous from BOTH sides: a 'fluffy' added to the schema's depth and a 'halo' added to the TypeScript focus each turn it red. The seed<->axes relationship is mechanical too — the four composite axes cannot drift because they are ONE definition with two users, and the ten scalars are held equal by a test, so 'the same vocabulary minus accent/document plus accent_hue/accent_chroma' is checked rather than commented. Both sides count fourteen. Every default is stated twice on purpose: as the `default` keyword for a tool, and as 'Default `x`.' in the description for the agent reading the generated markdown, with a test that fails on any axis whose prose forgets. The defaults are not invented — together they describe the shipped default theme, which is what makes { name, accent } a COMPLETE seed rather than a fragment, asserted directly. TWO DEVIATIONS from the task's sketch, both recorded: the axis sub-objects are $ref definitions rather than inline (that is what makes the shared vocabulary structural, and what lets the generated skill render each as its own table instead of the word 'object'), and themeAxes requires all fourteen keys — it is derived, so an incomplete block is exactly the drift the field exists to catch. Generated artifacts: gen:skill (references/manifest.md +165 lines; the Theme Manifest section now reads 'Required — all 9 / Optional — 6' with every axis, enum and default rendered from the schema's own strings), build:docs (333 files), and build:audit-browser, which the regeneration map does not list and the suite caught anyway — the bundle embeds src/protocol.ts and the diff is a pure minifier identifier swap at identical raw size. The spec page's schema paragraph was rewritten: it claimed the versioned and alias URLs are 'byte-identical while 1.0 is current', which stopped being true the moment 1.1 landed. check:manifest-api's recipes/table staleness re-verified pre-existing on a stashed tree — the same finding 1.1A-06 recorded.

A theme's axes become a FACT ABOUT ITS STYLESHEET. src/theme/axes.ts derives the fourteen axes of FAQIR-VISION §5.2 — 23 enumerated leaves plus accent_hue/accent_chroma — from CSS, gen:theme-manifests writes them into all 12 manifests (456 insertions, 12 deletions, every one the "preview" line gaining a comma), and the manifest gate re-derives and compares: the same rule tokens_overridden has followed since 0.4. Every threshold is a named exported constant with its rule beside it and is probed from BOTH sides. Tokens are read through buildSchemeLookups, the SAME cascade model the contrast gate uses, so the two gates cannot disagree about what --color-bg resolves to in a scheme. The one new piece of plumbing is resolveValue(), the non-colour twin of resolveColorString — that function stops at the first thing which parses as a colour, so it can never report 0.375rem or cubic-bezier(…). resolveValue follows a whole-value var() chain AND substitutes embedded ones, which is what lets `0 0 var(--border-width) 0` still read as a four-side shorthand; its own test caught the bug where the recursive tail resolve trimmed the separating space and turned four words into three. THE TABLE'S HEADLINE FINDING is §5.1's diagnosis restated as a number: FIFTEEN of the twenty-three enumerated leaves are IDENTICAL across all twelve themes (type.scale 1.2, type.base 16, the whole heading voice, shape.border, shape.corner, material, motion, density, focus, both decoration leaves, controls.input, controls.checkbox), four pairs are identical on EVERY one of them — aurora↔default, aurora↔slate, default↔slate, document↔document-serif differ only in accent — and 26 of the 66 pairs sit below §5.2's four-axis minimum. Pinned by a test, because 1.1A-14/15 exist to move it and 1.1A-12 arms the gate that forbids the low end. TWO DEVIATIONS from the task's sketch, both forced by tokens that shipped after it was written, both recorded at the constant: controls.button is `rect` only at a SQUARE corner (the sketch's "≥ --radius-lg soft, else rect" makes the shipped default theme derive `rect` at 6px against an 8px --radius-lg, while THEME_SEED_DEFAULTS records `soft` — a derived axis contradicting the seed defaults would mean { name, accent } is no longer the complete seed 1.1A-07 asserts), and controls.input is `filled` when --input-fill DIFFERS from --input-bg rather than "≠ none", because 1.1A-05 shipped it as var(--input-bg) and the sketch's rule would call every theme filled. Both are pinned by asserting axesFromCss(default.css) EQUAL to THEME_SEED_DEFAULTS — the first mechanical check of 1.1A-07's claim that the defaults describe the shipped default theme. Three judgement calls stated in code: type.pairing is `custom` when heading and body classify differently (the vocabulary names one class, and that is the exact inverse of the generator, which turns one pairing into both role tokens); material is read from the RAW var(--texture-<name>) because a texture resolves to a data URI and the name is the axis; density comes from a @ui:density header directive like @ui:schemes, since data-density is a subtree MODIFIER and density.css declares nothing at :root. tests/themes/axes.test.ts (150 cases) is the permanent gate: 94 fixtures, one per axis VALUE, with a meta-test proving coverage is complete rather than merely large; a boundary case at every threshold; both authoring forms shown to derive the same block, including a case whose dark side is deliberately below 15:1 so a :root-only parser would report `high` for both spellings; the table; the defaults; non-vacuity; the plumbing. manifest.test.ts gained the drift gate proven from three directions plus the converse, validateThemeAxes over every shipped block, and derived-scheme == hand-authored-scheme. No theme CSS was touched — no shipped theme wants a non-default density, so the @ui:density directive has no first user. check:manifest-api's recipes/table staleness is the pre-existing finding 1.1A-06/-07 recorded; this task touches no recipe controller.

The protocol grows two additive amendments in one session: data-skin, the fourth sanctioned token modifier, and data-density's third value, spacious. TokenModifier gains an open?: boolean field so a modifier can carry an open-ended vocabulary (a single <theme-name> placeholder) rather than a closed enum; data-skin is that modifier, landing alphabetically between data-motion and data-theme in TOKEN_MODIFIERS, purpose 'Selects which theme's token declarations a subtree resolves' for the scope selector 1.1A-19 will ship. SPEC-1.0.md's §4 table and prose grew to four modifiers, gained a data-skin example (scoping a card to the midnight theme) and a sentence naming data-skin's vocabulary open, and §8.2 gained the row the task named verbatim: 'Add a sanctioned token modifier that re-declares tokens only and names no component' / additive / 'It behaves exactly like the existing ones: no manifest, no per-component vocabulary, nothing published stops validating' — mirrored row-for-row into AMENDMENT_RULES. registry/tokens/density.css gains a third block, --density-scale: 1.25 with the control-height ramp at 36/44/52px — gentler than the x1.25 multiplier (40/50/60) would give, mirroring compact's asymmetry in the other direction: a roomy layout's controls grow slower than its padding. ONE COLLISION FOUND AND FIXED: data-skin's purpose text originally quoted the CLI flag as `faqir theme bundle --scope`, and the literal --scope substring inside prose was read by the shipped skill's token-reference regex (/--([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)/) as a declared custom property named 'scope', failing tests/generator/skill.test.ts's 'documents every declared token' gate — reworded to describe the flag rather than name it verbatim. tests/generator/layout-docs.test.ts carried its own hand-maintained duplicate of the sanctioned set (PROTOCOL_ATTRIBUTES plus three literal strings) that would have silently stayed at three; replaced with SANCTIONED_ATTRIBUTES from src/protocol.ts so there is one list rather than two that can drift. Six new tests: protocol-1.0.test.ts gained data-skin's open-vocabulary assertions (open: true, every other modifier open: falsy, isTokenModifier/mayTakeTierSuffix direct checks), the SANCTIONED_ATTRIBUTES growth count, and an auditHtmlSource check that a page combining data-skin and data-density="spacious" audits clean with no manifest for either; density.test.ts gained spacious's subtree-scoping pair (loosens a subtree, and nests compact inside spacious back down to compact's own ramp) and its 'remap is complete and derived' block now asserts SPACIOUS everywhere COMPACT/COMFORTABLE already were. Type a project can actually ship, and the refusal that makes it safe. src/fonts/catalog.ts pins 16 OFL families as 36 WOFF2 files — Inter, Geist, Manrope, DM Sans, Space Grotesk, Bricolage Grotesque, the three IBM Plex faces, Source Serif 4, Fraunces, Instrument Serif, Newsreader, Lora, Nunito, JetBrains Mono — each row carrying licence, the type class axesFromCss will report, the roles it suits, a fallback stack derived from its class, and per file an immutable version-pinned jsDelivr URL, the latin/latin-ext subset, the font-weight descriptor, the byte size and a SHA-256. Every pin was derived by downloading the file and checking three things before recording it: upstream declares OFL-1.1, the bytes start with wOF2, and the WOFF2 header's own length field equals the file's length. 13 families ship a variable-weight file (one request covers 100–900, or 100–1000 for DM Sans); the three static ones get 400 + 700, except Instrument Serif which is a single-weight display face. faqir fonts list|add|remove installs through a fetch seam that verifies EVERYTHING before a byte is written — bad hash, non-WOFF2, short file or dead URL each leave no files, no stylesheet and no config change, the all-or-nothing rule add --registry already follows — and hashes with sha256Hex out of utils/registry-index, i.e. node:crypto, so there is no new dependency and nothing new in the Node shim (fetch is global on Node >= 18, which is why runtime-shim.ts is untouched despite being in Touches). fonts.css is rendered WHOLE from an install list in faqir.config.json (fonts: [{ id, roles }]) rather than appended to, because appending cannot answer what remove takes out or what a second add does: from state both are free and add is idempotent by construction. A role has exactly ONE family — --font-body is one declaration — so assigning a role takes it off whoever held it and a family left with no roles leaves the list, keeping its files until removed by name. The rendered sheet is one @font-face per subset (font-display: swap, a unicode-range so an ASCII page never fetches latin-ext, a weight RANGE where the family ships one file) plus a :root block naming --font-heading/-body/-ui/-mono; the theme file is never edited, and the bundler inlines fonts.css immediately after tokens/theme.css so those role tokens win at equal specificity. A fonts.css without the managed header is the user's and is refused by both subcommands rather than overwritten. doctor re-hashes every file the stylesheet names — a missing font renders in the fallback face, so nothing else would say so — and flags a swap, a deletion, or a config recording a family with no stylesheet. Four families needed the FAMILY_CLASSES row §5.5 asks for (Bricolage Grotesque and IBM Plex Sans -> sans-grotesque, IBM Plex Serif -> serif-editorial, Instrument Serif -> serif-modern); gen:theme-manifests re-derived all 27 manifests with zero changes, since no shipped theme names any of them. Two things outside the plan's letter: the bundler now re-bases url("fonts/...") when bundle.output is outside output_dir, because inlining moves a stylesheet's relative urls and a 404 for a font is invisible; and the test fixture is Instrument Serif's two REAL faces (32 KB), because the installer verifies against the pinned hash and a synthetic fixture could only ever test the refusal path — serving the real bytes checks one family's pins against upstream on every run. tests/commands/fonts.test.ts (46 cases) is the permanent gate, and its class cross-check was proven non-vacuous by mis-declaring Fraunces as serif-modern and watching it fail by name. Verified on the artefact users run, not only in-suite: node dist/faqir.mjs fonts add fraunces --role heading downloaded and wrote both files at their pinned hashes over the live network, the bundle put fonts.css between the theme and the reset, doctor caught a one-byte tamper and exited 1, and remove took the family, its directory and the stylesheet back out. Follow-up 1.1A-30 records the one dead declaration found on the way: a theme manifest's fonts field has no writer, so theme-preview.ts's fontsHref branch is unreachable.

Scoped themes: `faqir theme bundle <name> --scope` rewrites a theme's :root and [data-theme] blocks onto a data-skin subtree — prelude-only edits over a parsed stylesheet, the scope root restating the five properties reset.css puts on :root/html/body, all 27 themes gated and three skins proved in Chromium to render exactly what they render at page level.

Every surface an agent reads now describes a theme by its fourteen derived axes instead of by adjective, and all of them render through one module: src/theme/describe.ts turns a manifest's axes block into table cells (twelve columns that with scheme make the fourteen), a vocabulary table (every leaf once, with its generate flag, values and default), a one-line summary, and the chips/attributes the gallery filters on. README's Theme System section was rewritten around two generated blocks kept current by a new gen:theme-docs / check:theme-docs gate (wired into release preflight and the regeneration map) plus a light-dark() subsection; CONTRIBUTING documents the five schema-1.1 fields and the seed workflow; the skill's theme table gained the axis columns and a 'Choosing a Theme by Axes' section the frontmatter promises; faqir context writes Axes/Seed/Nearest lines into context.md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt and the cursor rules; faqir_theme_info summaries carry kind, axes and distinctiveness and a new faqir_theme_list filters by dotted axis path, mood and kind, refusing unknown paths or values with the vocabulary named rather than returning an empty list a typo could hide in; the docs gallery shows nine axis chips per card and nine native selects that offer only values some shipped theme lands on, with a live count and an empty state, in gallery.js by attribute comparison alone. The a11y suite's new docs__themes_axis_filter case was run in local Chromium (2 passed) alongside axe scans of the gallery and home pages; the faqir audit gate caught one real mistake on the way (a five-column grid the vocabulary does not allow). Full suite 5822 pass / 12 skip / 0 fail, typecheck green.

@faqir-ui/rules: the zero-dependency, isomorphic shape validator — closed JSON Schema subset, nine format checkers, the message chain shared with faqir-validate, and a coercion pass that un-flattens the dotted names forms emit. A 93-case authored golden corpus is replayed in a happy-dom realm and in plain Bun and diffed case by case. Also reconciled the 14 typecheck errors inherited from 1.1A-20, output-neutrally.

The verbs and the logic under them. logic.js implements the 31-operator JSONLogic subset plus the two Faqir ops (date, regex) and refuses everything else by name; conformance is run, not claimed — the public suite is vendored (tests/vendor/jsonlogic-tests.json, SHA-256 and provenance recorded) and its 278 vectors partitioned: 249 implementable ones each get a case and must match, 29 naming map/filter/reduce/merge/?: must be refused with an error naming the operator, both halves asserted non-empty so nothing drifts into the ignored bucket. rules.js adds the five verbs with one documented pass order — computes in dependency order (the DAG comes from literal var paths, sorted once at compile time, a cycle naming its ids), then show (AND) and require (OR), then shape validation with that requiredness folded in, then hidden-field suppression by path prefix, then cross-field rules in document order, then jump as { from: to }. Two decisions carry the no-silent-failure invariant: a cross-field rule is SKIPPED while its own declared field is blank (required is the rule that should complain) but always runs on an undeclared path; and sync validate cannot run remote rules and does not pretend to — their ids come back in the verdict's new `pending`, a pending verdict is not valid, and validateAsync throws rather than skipping when no resolver was given, with a rejection or any non-verdict answer becoming a remote-error finding. The verdict gained `next` and `pending`; the corpus went 93 → 136 cases (golden/rules.json is 41, authored not captured). DefinitionError moved to errors.js and the bounds to limits.js so logic/rules can report without importing the shape validator; shape.js's validate became shapeFindings and rules.js owns the public compile/validate. The isomorphism gate now runs the bare-bun child under a different TZ, which is what proves date parses ISO 8601 itself rather than through Date.parse — and its import scan needed a lookbehind, since ["id", "jump", "from", "when"] was matching as an import of ", " (re-proved non-vacuous by planting a node:fs import). 360 new tests; full suite 6396 pass / 12 skip (unchanged) / 0 fail.
Faqir.validate registry + async validators; l-validate:<name>.async, the validating state, and the plugin reporting seam

The rules a form obeys in the page, from the same evaluator a server runs. `l-rules` reads a definition (a selector to a `<script type="application/json">`, or an expression in scope), compiles it once, and applies the six verbs to the DOM on init and on every delegated `input`/`change`: a hidden field's field-group takes `hidden` and its controls `disabled` — which is what makes the two verdicts comparable, since `FormData` then carries exactly what a server receives — `require` toggles `required`/`aria-required`, `compute` writes the scope and the control, `jump` lands in a reactive `$rules.next`, and both `validate` forms go through `Faqir.validate.register` so they run at faqir-validate's moments with its messages and its `validating` state; the plugin owns no message and paints no error of its own. Every attribute it touches is OWNED rather than assumed (three WeakSets and a WeakMap): a `hidden` the page wrote survives a rule that says "shown", and `required` is the OR of the markup's own and the rule's — a rule may add a demand, never lift one. The plugin IS `@faqir-ui/rules`, bundled: `scripts/build-rules-plugin.mjs` compiles `packages/rules/src/plugin.js` into the committed, byte-compare-gated `registry/core/plugins/faqir-rules.js`, header lifted from the source so the skill documents it from one place. 38 golden-corpus cases are replayed through rendered forms in two halves — the data round-trip read off the real `FormData` before the plugin writes anything, then `visible`/`required`/`computed`/`next`/findings as applied to the DOM — which is the browser/server parity claim made literal rather than asserted. Two deliberate deviations, both measured: the gzip budget is 11 KB and not the plan's 6 (the evaluator alone is 8.29 KB, the glue 1.93, total 10.31; the 6 predates the evaluator and the only way under it is a second implementation), enforced from both sides in `tests/build/check-size.test.ts`; and there is no `module.exports = install`, because `bun build --format=iife` resolves the free `module` identifier in its own scope and the line survived as dead code that looked alive (`require()` answered `{}`) — bundlers use the new `@faqir-ui/rules/plugin` export instead. Three real bugs fell out of writing it: a frozen `Object.freeze` constant behind `$rules` threw a TypeError under the scope Proxy (a Proxy may not wrap a non-configurable, non-writable property) in exactly the case it existed to make harmless; the first draft reported a documented form-level check as an absent field, i.e. flagged correct markup; and a definition embedded in a `<script type="application/json">` needs `<` escaped as `\u003c` or the element's raw text is truncated — filed as follow-up 1.1B-09 for the emitter to own. `l-rules` joined `PLUGIN_DIRECTIVES` so the audit does not call it unknown, the isomorphism gate now names `plugin.js` as the one host-coupled module in `src/` with the exemption asserted to be in use, `check:rules-plugin` joined the preflight, and the skill, docs site and `cdn.json` were regenerated. Full suite green (6,503 + 58 pass, 0 fail, the same 12 pre-existing skips); `check:manifest-api` is still red on the same nine recipe manifests, untouched here and tracked as 1.1B-08.
`faqir rules lint` and a published `rules.schema.json`: seven lint rules in the package, the schema as code beside it, and an accept/reject corpus that holds the two readings together.

The form and the rules it obeys, emitted together. `renderForm` gains `opts.rules` — a definition or the parts of one — and writes it beside the form as `<script type="application/json" id="<idPrefix>-rules">` with `l-rules="#<idPrefix>-rules"` on the `<form>` and `faqir-rules.js` in the `@ui:requires` line. Four conditional keywords the root schema may now carry stop throwing and become rules instead of being ignored: `if`/`then`/`else` and an `allOf` of conditionals derive `show` + `require`, `dependentRequired` derives one `require` per dependent (`{"!": {"missing": [trigger]}}` — presence in the package's own terms, so an unchecked box and an empty box both read false), and a wizard step's `when` derives the `jump` that steps over the page. `fields` is always DERIVED, never authored: the coercion type is the one the widget was chosen from, `step` arrives as the `multipleOf` the types always said it aliased, and `default` is dropped rather than handed over — the rules package would enforce it as a constraint. Author fields merge over the derived map, author rules come first (a `jump` contest is won by the first match), and their ids are reserved before a derived one is allocated. Three shapes are refused rather than half-honoured: a `then` property carrying keywords (a conditional CONSTRAINT, which `show` cannot express — it points at `opts.rules`), an `allOf` entry that is not a conditional, and a `when` on the first step, the last step, or two steps running. The wizard's navigation moved with the jumps, because emitting one nothing reads would be a new feature failing silently: with any jump in the definition `l-validate` asks `$rules.next[step]` instead of adding one, and Back reads the same answer in reverse (`next[step - 2] == step`) so it steps over a skipped page rather than landing on it. `<` is escaped to `\u003c` in the emitted JSON — the emitter half of follow-up 1.1B-09, and mandatory: a script element is raw text and `{"<=": …}` is what a definition is made of. 26 new tests in `packages/forms/tests/rules.test.ts`: emission shape, one case per derived construct, ten refusal paths, `lintDefinition` (the function behind `faqir rules lint`) asserted to report an EMPTY finding list for every definition emitted, and an end-to-end trio booting the generated drops — core, validate, rules, evaluated rather than require()d so `tests/core/faqir-rules.test.ts` keeps the first-require registration it asserts on — that watches a conditional field flip hidden/disabled/required, a dependent become required as its trigger is typed into, and a submit carry step 0 to step 2 with Back returning over the skip. Two golden files pin the bytes (`conditional-rules.html`, `wizard-jump.html`), both at zero audit findings with the `<script>` in them; the eighteen existing goldens and the `form-page` pattern are byte-identical, since nothing is emitted unless a form has rules. 6941 pass / 0 fail; no dependency added — the renderer writes the definition, it never evaluates one.

Rules documented from generated data, not restated: $rules joins the plugin's @ui:provides, plugins declare their modifiers the way the engine does, README gains a Validation section, security.md §4.1 says what a remote rule actually sends, and @faqir-ui/rules joins the release lockstep.

Night Shift v0: the framework generates while nobody is watching, and the rules of the shift are code rather than prose. `/faqir-dream` does one dream per run and its ONLY job is the part that needs taste — read the brief, write the seed; everything after is `scripts/dream/theme.mjs`, which branches, runs nine gates in order, checks the diff and commits, or discards and says why. Every subprocess goes through one injected runner, so `tests/dream/theme-dream.test.ts` watches the whole pipeline against a fake repository and a stubbed generator: the gate order read back, the four generated files, the scorecard, TWO commits (a ledger row cannot cite a hash it is inside — the shape /faqir-plan already uses), and the discard paths, which are the half worth proving. The gate list is the plan's plus one it forgot: `gen:theme-docs`, because README's theme tables are a committed artifact and a new theme without it leaves check:theme-docs red and the PR un-mergeable. Shipping it surfaced what a theme dream ACTUALLY touches — `gen:theme-manifests` exits non-zero for a theme with no editorial seed and `gen:theme-previews` for one with no gallery spec, so the allow-list has to admit two source files, and the guards test asserts both refusals against the generators rather than trusting the note. Guards (`guards.mjs`, 61 cases): clean tree, never a commit on main, a git subcommand allow-list with push/merge/rebase absent, `git clean -x` refused in every spelling including `-fdx`, never `--allow-similar` (distinctiveness IS the keep condition), and the whole diff classified BEFORE the commit — forbidden-by-name separated from outside-the-allow-list, because the two need different answers. The twelve briefs were aimed by measurement: the queue test scores every axes_hint against all 24 shipped axis blocks and failed three of them at 2, 3 and 3 differing leaves (moss, arcade, porcelain), which is how they came to sit at 4–13; three more cases refuse the vocabulary values that render nothing (1.1A-16's corner-under-sharp, 1.1A-25's small-caps, 1.1A-26's double divider). `dreams.tsv` is autoresearch's format plus date/kind/branch/gates/taste, append-only asserted on the BYTES already on disk, and a tab in a cell is a refusal rather than an escape. 179 tests, zero dependencies; the snapshot pair was proven for real (a genuinely dark dark shot of editorial) while nothing under `bun run test` launches a browser. 13 full runs: 12 green, the 13th the l-cloak flake 1.1A-23 tracks — control arm with the new files moved aside went 5/5, which separates nothing at 1-in-13 against the clean tree's own 1-in-9.

Cadence: nightly.sh runs one dream in a disposable worktree (the branch survives, the bundle is harvested, a dirty worktree is kept rather than deleting a discard's row); digest.mjs renders DREAMS.md from the ledger unioned with every unmerged dream branch; docs/dream-rubric.md v1.0 is the versioned five-criterion rubric, with its prose and its code asserted against each other.

Release 1.1 "Personality": seven packages at 1.1.0 in lockstep, @faqir-ui/rules published for the first time. Getting there took a whole-tree review (docs/code-evaluation-1.1.md, 29 findings) and a fix pass: prototype pollution in coerce, catastrophic `pattern` regexes (nested and bounded repeats, overlapping alternation, plus a 10,000-character subject cap), repair fixes that never applied or hit the wrong element, output paths that escaped the project (now one helper, src/utils/paths.ts), the l-for duplicate-key leak, and the 1.0 upgrade path, where `faqir upgrade` now merges the token layer and base styles as well as the components. The rehearsal was green at cc4bf57: 14/14 gates, 264 test files, and the packed CLI answering under Node and Bun.
